before.value: Pending records can usually be corrected by the original submitter or repository staff; approved records should be corrected by authorized staff or the original contributor if they have the proper role; records later found inaccurate should be directly intervened on by repository staff. Staff who can correct and moderate records themselves may edit normal bibliographic fields and moderate records still in draft, pending, or otherwise not yet finalized. Once a record is approved or published, changes to key fields or the attached full text should require a second review, especially if they affect the public record or reporting; unresolved conflicts should be flagged for another moderator or escalated to a higher authority rather than guessed. For duplicate/mismatch review, the moderator should compare the title, authors, DOI, year, venue, and any attached full text side by side, along with whichever fields the system thinks are uncertain. If the DOI matches exactly, that is a strong signal to treat it as the same publication, but the moderator should still confirm before merging. If the evidence is weak or conflicting, it should stay unresolved and be routed to a more experienced reviewer or escalated for manual checking. When duplicate records have weak or conflicting evidence, low-confidence matches with no critical impact can stay in a review queue for later; high-priority records, records with conflicting identifiers, or cases where there is a risk of merging the wrong publication or author should be escalated immediately to a more experienced reviewer. It should not automatically overwrite the record when new metadata appears; instead it should mark the record as having new evidence or a pending update, keep the migration flag until someone reviews it, and let a moderator decide whether to accept the correction to preserve the audit trail. Missing mandatory fields should reject the record from the main import and keep it in an error report or staging area for fix-and-reimport. Duplicates should not create a second record blindly; they should either link to the existing record or be flagged for review depending on how strong the match is. Ambiguous values may be imported as uncertain only if they can be clearly marked; otherwise they should remain in a manual review queue. Duplicate records affecting already published, widely cited, or reporting-linked items should be escalated sooner, especially when conflicting identifiers point to different authors or institutions. Simple uncertainty in a new or low-impact record can stay in the normal review queue if the reviewer can leave it untouched and move on. Only cases with clear publication-risk, such as a possible merge that could corrupt the official bibliographic record, should go to the more experienced reviewer immediately.

before.value: Do not merge name variants automatically just because they look similar; require an approved authority record or at least manual confirmation before treating different spellings or forms as the same author, to avoid collapsing distinct people, especially with common names or transliterated forms. Keep the source form in the record, but normalize it into a standard authority form when there is a confirmed match; if confidence is not sufficient, keep records separate and flag them for review rather than forcing normalization. For similar-looking matches, do not auto-link unless confidence is high and the matching rules are very clear; otherwise leave them unnormalized and send them to manual review. Auto-link only for agreed-safe cases such as exact variants or well-known standardized abbreviations. Auto-linking should be limited to cases where the match is essentially deterministic, like an exact normalized variant, a known abbreviation that’s already approved, or a transliteration that maps unambiguously to one authority form. If there is any real ambiguity, especially with common abbreviations or names that could belong to more than one person or institution, it should go to manual review.
